desired_outcome: Prevent Skill Factory and Skills SDK candidates from advancing without deterministic evidence for routing, release gates, scenario parity, security risk modes, plugin shape, advisory closure, and repair-loop monotonicity.
user_specific_constraints: Use the testing, improve-agent-native, sdk-scenario-generator, evals-router, and improve-codebase-architecture skills as the governing lenses.
Promote repeated steering into validators, tests, rubrics, or durable evidence surfaces rather than adding prose-only reminders.
Keep package-shape validation separate from release-readiness validation.
Do not allow advisory or warning findings to carry into later eval phases.
Do not move from oss-local to oss-cloud or Tessl without release-lane evidence.
copied_assumption_rejected: A skill package that passes package verify is not automatically ready for release-lane movement or Tessl evaluation.
fundamental_constraints: Release movement must be evidence-led and ordered.
Scenarios used by SDK, OSS, and Tessl lanes must be traceable to the same canonical case set.
Security, prompt-injection, data-boundary, and destructive-command risks must be explicit package gates.
Skill Factory routes must choose the correct create, install, build, refactor, or improve surface without prompt wording drift.
Repair loops must classify regressions before another edit pass.
smallest_effective_mechanism: Add focused validator checks and regression tests to existing Skills SDK release-ratchet, Skill Factory overlay, and route-selection surfaces.
rejected_alternatives: Rely on operator memory or thread instructions to remember the lane order.
Add a new checklist without executable enforcement.
Treat Tessl live scoring as the first place to detect package, scenario, security, or route drift.
Patch only the current skill scenarios without adding anti-regression tests.
evidence_required: Standalone Skill Factory overlay semantic validator covers SDK ladder, construction contract, and gold rubric wiring.
Release-ratchet validator blocks missing factory-gate, gate-chain, scenario-parity, security, plugin-shape, advisory, and repair-loop evidence.
Route-selection tests prove external installs, refactors, plugin work, and improve-existing requests do not drift to the wrong factory surface.
Focused tests prove each new ratchet fails on the intended missing or malformed evidence.
A real package check demonstrates package verification remains separate from release-ratchet evidence.
